Rand Paul makes the case against Presidential powers to declare unlimited and perpetual wars

In September of 2001, a bill passed into law approving the "war on terrorism." It was called the 2001 AUMF, Authorization for Use of Military Force, and was supposedly directed at Afghanistan. Obama has recently used this same authorization to expand wars. This is the 'unlimited and perpetual wars' law.

One person in the House stood completely alone in voting against this bill -- California Representative Barbara Lee.
Why even have such provisions if you can passut once and it's good forever?

Lawyers have a saying I've heard a few times now: "bad facts make for bad law." It means that when faced with a particularly atrocious situation that the current law cannot remedy, those in power will do almost anything to remedy it, even if it means changing the law in a way that turns out to be disastrous in the future.

9/11 is perhaps the truest application of this saying in modern history. Most people were completely unwilling to accept that our laws at the time, which both allowed for freedom from state intrusions into private life and made declaring wars difficult, would allow something like that to happen and then add insult to injury by putting roadblocks in the way of chasing after those responsible. In the fervor to hunt them down and never allow it to happen again, they forgot that those rules, harsh consequences and all, were a big part of what made this nation great in the first place.

Not many people know that Alabama vs. Tennessee (i.e. the "Third Saturday in October") has been played since 1901, and a lot of Alabama fans hate Tennessee more than Auburn because of how that rivalry played out in the late 90s. Alabama is also a pretty hated rival (especially recently) among Mississippi teams - MSU since 1896 and Ole Miss since 1894. While Auburn vs. Georgia is the 2nd most important rivalry on the plains, Auburn is also rivals with two other Tigers (LSU and Clemson), and the AU/FL game was a headline event in the 2000s. Florida vs Tennessee, Arkansas vs. LSU, etc. are all underappreciated rivalries that have helped shape the conference.
